newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Qantas to double flights into China.
newsitem.headline: Qantas to double flights into China.

text.p: Qantas Airways is to double its flights into China from two to four per week because of increasing passenger demand, an airline spokesman has told Reuters.
The increased Sydney, Shanghai, Beijing, Shanghai, Sydney schedule will begin in August, 12 months after Qantas inaugurated its Shanghai service, he added.

Three Boeing 767-300 aircraft, which have been specially upgraded to carry more payload, are being utilised but Peter Barry, the airline's regional freight manager said he does not expect the increased service to have a big impact on the freight market between the two countries .

"This is a passenger led development and we don't expect to see a dramatic increase in the amount of freight carried. Other airlines such as China Eastern are wanting to fly the route and I think with the competition hotting up it is a case of everyone getting a slice of the cake rather than the cake getting bigger," Barry told Reuters in an interview from his Singapore headquarters.

Barry said the ex-China freight market had been "pretty good with no complaints" since Qantas started flying to Shanghai last year. Between six to eight tonnes of belly cargo can be carried and the main goods carried down under from Shanghai were high-tech products and garments. Cargo load factors were in the "70 per cent margin", Barry added.

Qantas rivals Ansett Australia also plan to start a twice weekly Sydney-Shanghai service using Boeing 767-300ER aircraft from June, according to an airline spokeswoman in Hong Kong. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+ 5017
